pullRequest.title: Document search operator support in `gh search` help
pullRequest.body:
<!--

change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

The `--help` output of `gh search issues` and `gh search prs` lacked information on using boolean operators (`OR`, `AND`) and parentheses for nesting.

For the operators to work, they must be passed as separate argument, rather than inside a multi-word quoted sting (in which case they get interpreted as plain words), otherwise and the search can omit relevant results (or return nothing at all) without signaling usage of unsupported syntax.

I decided to contribute this info to the `--help` output of those commands, so that others (and my future self! 😅) could know how to proceed in case they bump into this issue.

### How did you test this change?

This change only affects help text; no behavior is changed. I verified that the output matches the expected by checking the rendered help output:
- `go run ./cmd/gh search issues --help`
- `go run ./cmd/gh search prs --help`

Just to be sure, I also confirmed that the relevant tests still pass, with `go test ./pkg/cmd/search/issues/ ./pkg/cmd/search/prs/`.

commit.messageHeadline: Document search operator support in `gh search` help
commit.messageBody:
The `--help` output of `gh search issues` and `gh search prs`
lacked information on using boolean operators (`OR`, `AND`)
and parentheses for nesting. Each operator must be passed as separate arguments;
wrapping a whole query string in quotes makes it match as a single literal phrase,
so the operators are treated as plain words,
and the search will fail to capture relevant results
rather than reporting usage of unsupported syntax.

This patch updates the help text to make this nuance explicit to users.

🛑 Requirement: Scope this guidance to advanced-search-capable API calls

This is true for the default API search only when the host supports advanced issue search. On older GHES versions the searcher falls back to the legacy syntax, and `--web` always opens the legacy global search, where these operators and nesting are unsupported. As written, users on those paths are told that merely splitting the query into arguments enables functionality that the selected backend cannot parse.

nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Do not claim pull-request searches lack advanced syntax

The default `gh search prs` path uses the same advanced issue-search REST backend as `gh search issues` and appends `type:pr`; the merged implementation in cli/cli#11638 explicitly verified `advanced_search=true` for this command. This text therefore directs users away from supported `AND`/`OR` and nested queries on github.com and GHES 3.18+, although `--web` and older hosts still use the legacy syntax.
